source.title: The impact of global signal regression on resting state correlations: are anti-correlated networks introduced?

confidence_rationale: The strongest and most decision-relevant literature finding for SD-079, and it cuts both ways. It confirms that removing a shared common mode from a set of signals is a decisive, non-cosmetic operation that transforms an inflated all-positive similarity distribution into a differentiated one -- SD-079's central mechanism. But it also establishes ANALYTICALLY, not merely empirically, that after such a removal the similarity values must sum to a negative value and are distributed approximately centred on zero. That makes the specific downstream evidence SD-079 cites for success -- that the MECH-292 goal_match_floor now excludes 9 of 24 anchors and the MECH-339 outshining gate is now nonzero on 9 of 24 -- partly a mathematical consequence of centering rather than a demonstration that those absolute gates now select on motivational relevance. Confidence held at 0.62: source quality is high and the analytic component transfers exactly, but the empirical apparatus (BOLD, seed-voxel correlation, breath-holding) is far from a hippocampal anchor pool, so transfer risk is substantial.
failure_signatures: After subtraction of a common mode, the similarity values to a given reference must sum to a negative value, and the empirical distribution of those values becomes bell-shaped and centred on zero. Any ABSOLUTE threshold applied downstream of centering therefore partitions the pool at a location largely determined by the centering operation itself, not by the content of the cue -- so 'the gate is now live' and 'the gate is now meaningful' are different claims, and only the first is demonstrated by an exclusion count.

Negative similarity values produced by centering can be spurious: the paper shows in simulation that small phase differences between signals are sufficient to produce negative correlations after global regression, and concludes that global signal regression is most likely the cause of the anti-correlated networks previously interpreted as intrinsic brain organisation. The analogous REE risk is that centered goal_match values below zero are read as active dissimilarity between a goal and an anchor when they encode nothing of the sort.

The interpretation of any structure discovered only after common-mode removal is called into question by this paper's central argument. A REE result of the form 'the centered arm shows differentiation that the raw arm does not' is necessary but not sufficient; it needs a check that the differentiation tracks something independently identifiable, not merely that it exists.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Global signal regression -- removing the whole-brain average BOLD time series from each voxel prior to computing functional connectivity -- has a mathematically necessary consequence: after regression, correlation values to a seed voxel must sum to a negative value. Simulations show that small phase differences between regions alone can produce spurious negative correlations. A combined breath-holding and visual task experiment shows that the relative phase of global and local signals affects connectivity measures, and that experimentally, global signal regression produces bell-shaped correlation distributions centred on zero. Analyses of negatively correlated resting-state networks indicate global signal regression is most likely the cause of the observed anti-correlations, which calls into question the interpretation of negatively correlated brain regions when global signal regression is used as an initial processing step.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-079 subtracts a slow EMA common-mode baseline from z_goal before Anchor.goal_match, on the diagnosis that the raw match spans only ~0.011 across a 24-anchor pool so the MECH-292 goal_match_floor excludes nothing and the MECH-339 outshining gate clip((0.5 - goal_match)/0.5) is identically zero. This paper is the closest external precedent for exactly that operation on exactly that kind of signal: a set of concurrently-measured channels sharing a large common component, where the common component inflates every pairwise similarity toward the ceiling and its removal restores a spread. It supports SD-079's diagnosis directly -- the shared component IS what is destroying the contrast, and subtracting it IS what restores it. Its warning maps onto the part of SD-079 that is load-bearing for downstream claims: because centering necessarily re-centres the match distribution near zero, the post-fix observations that the floor now excludes 9 of 24 and the gate is now nonzero on 9 of 24 are the expected arithmetic signature of centering ANY pool, and are therefore weak evidence that those gates now carry motivational-relevance information. The gate being live is established; the gate being informative is not, and this paper is why that distinction matters.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The analytic half of the result transfers cleanly and the empirical half does not. Murphy et al.'s sum-to-negative result is a property of removing a shared component from a set of signals and then correlating them, and REE's centered goal_match is that same construction, so the distributional consequence should be expected to hold. But everything establishing the SPURIOUSNESS of the resulting negative values is BOLD-specific: phase relationships between haemodynamic time series, breath-holding-induced global fluctuations, seed-voxel connectivity over a scan session. REE's z_goal is not a time series correlated against another time series; it is a single latent vector compared by cosine against stored anchor snapshots, so the phase argument has no direct analogue and the spuriousness finding transfers as a caution rather than as a prediction. There is also a real disanalogy in what the common mode IS: in fMRI it is contested whether the global signal is artefact or neural (see the sibling entry, and Billings & Keilholz 2018), whereas in REE the common mode is a known consequence of SD-008 z_world under-differentiation -- a defect being routed around, not a signal of uncertain status. That asymmetry makes REE's case for removal STRONGER than the fMRI case, and should be stated when citing this entry, so the caveat is not over-read as an argument against centering per se.
mapping.source_context: Human resting-state and task fMRI (BOLD), posterior cingulate seed-based functional connectivity, plus numerical simulation and a combined breath-holding / visual task paradigm; young adult participants; NIMH Section on Functional Imaging Methods.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality is high: a heavily-cited NeuroImage paper combining an analytic derivation, simulation, and a designed experiment, from a group with no stake in the outcome favouring either side of the anti-correlation debate. mapping_fidelity 0.60 is generous on the analytic result (which is essentially exact) and harsh on the empirical apparatus (which is not transferable), averaged. transfer_risk 0.50 reflects a genuine domain jump -- haemodynamic time series to latent-vector cosine -- partly offset by the fact that the load-bearing conclusion for REE is the distributional one, which is algebra rather than physiology. Aggregate 0.62 rather than higher because the entry's VALUE here is a caveat on interpretation rather than a confirmation, and a caveat whose empirical support does not transfer should not be weighted as though it did.
